newsitem.title: FRANCE: Don't link EU-Israel deal to settlement - minister.
newsitem.headline: Don't link EU-Israel deal to settlement - minister.

text.p: Foreign Minister Herve de Charette rejected on Wednesday a suggestion that France should link ratification of a European Union accord with Israel to halting a disputed new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
De Charette met later on Wednesday with Palestinian culture and information minister Yasser Abd Rabbo and expressed concern at the state of the Middle East peace process.
"There is serious worry among all those who are attached to the peace process," de Charette told reporters after the meeting.
He urged a resumption of Israeli-Palestinian peace talks and said the Oslo peace accord was the only road to peace.
The EU-Israel association agreement would give the Jewish state more favourable trade terms and open up new areas of economic and scientific cooperation with the 15-nation group.
"I know there is hesitation among you (about ratifying the accord)...but the government's position is that we must not give in to this temptation," de Charette told the National Assembly.

He was replying to centre-right parliamentarian Aymeri de Montesquiou, who said Paris should make ratification conditional on a halt to construction of the Har Homa housing project and resumption of talks on the basis of the Oslo peace accords and the principle of exchanging occupied land for peace.

The newspaper Le Monde said Palestinian envoy Leila Chahid had convinced ex-president Valery Giscard d'Estaing, chairman of the assembly's foreign affairs committee, to delay ratification until the Middle East situation calmed down.
It said National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin, a senior supporter of President Jacques Chirac, also favoured delay.

The government initially set a ratification debate for February 27 but it was postponed because of other legislation. Rescheduled for March 20, it was dropped from the agenda at the committee's initiative and parliament adjourns on Thursday for an Easter break until April 15.

De Charette said the Har Homa project was contrary to the Oslo accords and Israel's offer to evacuate just two percent of occupied West Bank land in its next redeployment was seen by Palestinians as a provocation.

"But France's mission is to work each day to help renew the dialogue between the parties...with determination but in the direction of peace," he said, condemning two attacks on Israeli civilians this month as unacceptable terrorism.
The minister said France would soon announce new initiatives concerning Israel-Palestinian relations as well as ties between Israel, Syria and Lebanon.
"We have a role to play together with others and we will not cease to act in favour of peace," he said.
